message.reasoning:
I am playing as player p3 in this Monopoly turn.

I am analyzing the board. I have $143 cash and a brown monopoly. Player 2 dominates with hotels and $426 cash. Players 1 and 4 are bankrupt. I just paid rent on Oriental Avenue and mortgaged Virginia Avenue.

I confirmed the cash math: $63 plus the $80 mortgage on Virginia yields $143. From Oriental Avenue, rolling a 2 lands on Connecticut Avenue with a $600 hotel rent, which is survivable. Rolling an 8 lands on the four railroads for $200, and rolling 11 or 12 lands on Tennessee or New York with one house each.

Mortgaging both Mediterranean and Baltic would raise cash to $203. That covers the $200 railroad rent and the orange house rents, but not the Connecticut hotel. I am weighing whether to mortgage now to survive the next rolls.

Rolling a 1 on Oriental lands on Vermont with a hotel. Rolling a 3 lands on St. Charles, which is unimproved because I own Virginia and p2 lacks a pink monopoly there, so rent is only $10. Rolling a 4 hits the Electric Company for $40. Rolling a 5 lands on States Avenue at base rent $12. Rolling a 6 lands on Virginia, which costs nothing.

Player 2's orange monopoly is unevenly built. Tennessee and New York each have one house, but St. James Place has none.

Rolling a 5 on Oriental lands on the Electric Company for $50. Rolling a 9 lands on St. James Place with no houses, which doubles the base rent to about $20. Rolling an 11 lands on Tennessee Avenue with one house, costing $70.

Rolling a 12 on Oriental lands on New York Avenue with one house for $80. The two hotel rolls are unavoidable deaths regardless of mortgages. The five railroads rolls kill me without mortgaging, and the three hotel rolls kill me either way. Mortgaging both brown properties raises cash to $203 and saves me from the railroad rent.

I will mortgage Mediterranean Avenue first, then Baltic Avenue next turn. Trading away brown properties is pointless because player 2 would not trade to keep me alive. Building houses on the browns costs $50 each, which I cannot afford with only $143.
